title: 118. End of the First World War & Remembrance

sentences.en: All she saw was a merciless sea of black crosses, bearing little strips of stamped tin at all angles across their faces.
sentences.zh: 她眼中所见，尽是无情的黑色十字架海洋，这些十字架以各种角度矗立着，上面钉着刻有文字的锡片。

sentences.en: She could distinguish no order or arrangement in their mass, nothing but a waist-high wilderness as of weeds stricken dead rushing at her.
sentences.zh: 她无法在这一片密集的墓碑中分辨出任何秩序或排列，只觉得那是一片齐腰高的荒野，仿佛杂草枯死后向她扑来。

sentences.en: She went forward, moved to the left and the right hopelessly, wondering by what guidance she should ever come to her own.
sentences.zh: 她向前走去，茫然地向左、向右移动，心中纳闷自己该循着什么指引才能找到亲人的墓地。

sentences.en: A great distance away, there was a line of whiteness.
sentences.zh: 在极远处，有一道白色的线条。

sentences.en: It proved to be a block of some two or three hundred graves, whose headstones had already been set, whose flowers were planted out and whose new-sown grass showed green.
sentences.zh: 那原来是两三百座坟墓组成的方阵，墓碑已经立好，花朵也已种下，新播的草坪显出点点绿意。

sentences.en: Here she could see clear-cut letters at the ends of the rose and, referring to her slip, realised that it was not here she must look.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她能看清玫瑰花丛尽头清晰的铭文，对照着手中的纸条，她意识到自己要找的并不是这里。

sentences.en: That is towards the end of a short story called The Gardener by Rudyard Kipling, and it describes a woman called Helen Terrell, a spinster,
sentences.zh: 那段文字出自鲁德亚德·吉卜林短篇小说《园丁》的结尾，讲述了一位名叫海伦·特雷尔的未婚女子，

sentences.en: who has brought up her nephew, who then enlists in the First World War, dies, and that describes her going to one of the war cemeteries that is in the process of being built.
sentences.zh: 她抚养长大的侄子在第一次世界大战中应征入伍并阵亡，那段描写的是她前往一座正在建设中的战争公墓的情景。

sentences.en: And Dominic, I know that you're an admirer of that short story because it packs an incredible punch at the end, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我知道你是那篇短篇小说的崇拜者，因为它结尾的冲击力极强，不是吗？

sentences.en: For reasons that I'm not going to explain.
sentences.zh: 原因我就不解释了。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: People, if you haven't read it, it's available online.
sentences.zh: 各位，如果还没读过，网上可以找到。

sentences.en: It's quite short.
sentences.zh: 篇幅很短。

sentences.en: I think it's one of the great short stories ever written.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是有史以来最伟大的短篇小说之一。

sentences.en: I couldn't agree more, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意，汤姆。

sentences.en: It's funny because you said to me you were going to go in on The Gardener,
sentences.zh: 真有意思，因为你之前跟我说你要讲《园丁》，

sentences.en: And I had been thinking, would I mention The Gardener in the podcast?
sentences.zh: 我当时还在想，我要不要在播客里提到《园丁》呢？

sentences.en: And I thought, I won't go into it in case Tom hasn't read it, and then I'll have to do all the carrying with it, and I might start crying.
sentences.zh: 后来我想，还是别提了，万一汤姆没读过，那我就得一个人撑起整个话题，而且我可能会讲着讲着就哭出来。

sentences.en: And that would be really...
sentences.zh: 那可真是……

sentences.zh: 你知道吗，多米尼克，我每年11月11日都会读一遍。

sentences.zh: 真的。

sentences.zh: 但我确实会读《园丁》，因为我总是想读读看，自己能不能在读到结尾时不热泪盈眶？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 目前为止，还没成功过。

sentences.zh: 对于那些认为吉卜林只会写《丛林奇谭》和那种帝国沙文主义的人，如果你读读这篇短篇小说，甚至花不了一个小时，

sentences.en: it will utterly dispel everything you thought about Kipling.
sentences.zh: 它会彻底颠覆你对吉卜林的所有看法。

sentences.en: Because Kipling, of course, had lost his son, Tom, hadn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为吉卜林当然也失去了他的儿子，汤姆，对吧？

sentences.en: John, loose in 1915.
sentences.zh: 约翰，1915年阵亡的。

sentences.en: And Kipling had pulled strings to get him into the army and then lost his son.
sentences.zh: 吉卜林动用关系让他参了军，结果却失去了儿子。

sentences.en: And the grief stayed with him for the rest of his...
sentences.zh: 那种悲痛伴随了他余生……

sentences.en: And one of the challenges, obviously, for people was to deal with the scale of the loss and the scale of the grief.
sentences.zh: 显然，人们面临的挑战之一，就是如何应对那场战争造成的巨大损失和沉重的悲痛。

sentences.en: And I think often, in terms of literature, it's a struggle for people.
sentences.zh: 我认为在文学层面，这往往是人们难以逾越的障碍。

sentences.en: But I think the Kipling story is...
sentences.zh: 但我认为吉卜林的故事是……

sentences.zh: 我认为这是专门探讨这一主题的最伟大的文学作品。

sentences.zh: 汤姆，我认为有两部伟大的文学作品，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 除了吉卜林的短篇小说，还有一本新书，我想。

sentences.zh: 是不是有一本关于这个主题的新书？

sentences.zh: 抱歉，多米尼克。

sentences.en: God, here I am.
sentences.zh: 天哪，你看我。

sentences.en: Here I am dwelling on Kipling, who's been long dead.
sentences.zh: 你看我还在纠结于早已作古的吉卜林。

sentences.en: But, of course, the top historian has written...
sentences.zh: 不过，当然了，那位顶尖历史学家写了……

sentences.zh: 死者的话题就到此为止吧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Let's cut to the living.
sentences.zh: 让我们转入正题，谈谈活着的人。

sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我听说你出了一本关于第一次世界大战的新书。

sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's one of my Adventures in Time series about the First World War, and I promise we won't talk about it too much.
sentences.zh: 这是我《时间冒险》系列中关于一战的一本，我保证我们不会过多谈论它。

sentences.en: Is it very moving?
sentences.zh: 它很感人吗？

sentences.en: So I think I found it quite moving to write it, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我觉得写这本书的过程挺感人的。

sentences.en: I found it genuinely moving.
sentences.zh: 我感到发自内心的触动。

sentences.en: And the First World War is, like all wars, it's a mosaic of incredibly stirring and emotive individual stories.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战就像所有战争一样，是由无数令人动容、情感充沛的个人故事拼凑而成的马赛克。

sentences.en: And writing it for children, I was particularly conscious of that, because, of course, the First World War is presented to children as the sort of abyss of suffering.
sentences.zh: 为孩子们写这本书时，我特别注意到了这一点，因为一战在孩子们眼中通常被呈现为苦难的深渊。

sentences.en: So, yeah, but enough of that.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，这些就说这么多。

sentences.en: So you can obviously buy it for your children, and you should for Christmas.
sentences.zh: 你可以给孩子们买这本书，圣诞节送给他们再合适不过了。

sentences.en: But we want to talk more broadly, don't we, about the end of the war and how it was remembered.
sentences.zh: 但我们想更广泛地谈谈战争的结束以及人们是如何纪念它的，对吧？

sentences.en: So why don't we, before we get into the remembrance itself, just start, why don't we start sort of on the last day?
sentences.zh: 那么，在进入纪念活动本身之前，我们为什么不从最后一天开始讲起呢？

sentences.en: So...
sentences.zh: 那么……

sentences.en: Yes, a kind of sequel to the Gary Sheffield episode.
sentences.zh: 是的，算是加里·谢菲尔德那期节目的续篇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: About the Western Front.
sentences.zh: 关于西线战场。

sentences.en: So the Germans have been...
sentences.zh: 当时德国人已经……

sentences.en: They've launched their Great Gamble, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 他们发起了“大赌博”，不是吗？

sentences.en: And they've been pushed back.
sentences.zh: 结果被击退了。

sentences.en: And everything's falling apart in Germany.

sentences.zh: 德国革命已经爆发。

sentences.zh: 他们已经派特使前往贡比涅森林与盟军谈判。

sentences.zh: 现在是11月11日，星期一。

sentences.zh: 我们可以从凌晨5点19分开始，那是特使们……

sentences.en: They've heard reports.
sentences.zh: 他们听到了报告。

sentences.en: So these are MPs, right?
sentences.zh: 这些人是议员，对吧？

sentences.zh: 是的，他们是政客。

sentences.en: There's, I think, a couple of sort of military guys.
sentences.zh: 我想还有几个军方的人。

sentences.en: There's, they have been sort of sent.
sentences.zh: 他们是被派去的。

sentences.en: They have the, the regime is collapsing behind them.
sentences.zh: 他们身后的政权正在崩溃。

sentences.en: So the Kaiser has fled.
sentences.zh: 所以德皇逃跑了。

sentences.zh: 德皇是在周六晚上到周日早上逃走的。

sentences.en: To the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 逃往了荷兰。

sentences.en: So it's now Monday.
sentences.zh: 现在是星期一。

sentences.en: They've discovered, they see from the French Royal Women's newspapers that the Kaiser has abdicated and Germany is in revolution.
sentences.zh: 他们从法国报纸上得知德皇已经退位，德国正在发生革命。

sentences.en: They've been given a few days to consider the Allies' terMs.
sentences.zh: 他们被给了几天时间考虑盟军的条款。

sentences.en: And they basically decide they have no choice but to accept them.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上决定别无选择，只能接受。

sentences.en: So they gather in Marshall Foch's carriage in this forest, in this forest clearing, very bleary-eyed, just round about dawn, before dawn, I think.
sentences.zh: 于是他们在森林里的一节火车车厢里聚集，在福煦元帅的指挥下，在黎明时分，我想是在黎明前，他们睡眼惺忪。

sentences.en: And they end up signing the terms that basically say hostilities will cease at 11th of November, i.e. on Monday, at 11 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 最终他们签署了条款，规定敌对行动将于11月11日，也就是周一，11点停止。

sentences.en: They have to give a time, obviously, a random time.
sentences.zh: 他们显然得定个时间，一个随机的时间。

sentences.en: And so they choose it for the symmetry of it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们选择了这个时间，为了对称性。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, also because that will give to everybody, that will give time for the news to spread across the front.

Yeah.

Yeah, I suppose of the 11th.

sentences.zh: 因为法国人和美国人尤其不信任德国人，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, also there's an inbuilt ratchet, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且有一种内在的惯性，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你感到恐惧，如果你认为敌人有可能继续战斗，那你就会继续战斗。

sentences.en: So it depends slightly where you are on the front.
sentences.zh: 所以这取决于你在前线的具体位置。

sentences.zh: 但基本上，在那几个小时里，

sentences.en: I mean, it's extraordinary to think of.
sentences.zh: 想到这一点真是令人震惊。

sentences.zh: 想象一下，在10点钟死去，你知道吗？

sentences.zh: 确实有人在10点45分左右阵亡，诸如此类。

sentences.zh: 他活了下来。

sentences.zh: 他活了下来。

sentences.en: That's gutting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那真是太令人沮丧了，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，确实有一些非常令人心碎的故事。

sentences.zh: 还有个法国人，奥古斯丁·特雷布雄。

sentences.zh: 10点45分，他的指挥官给了他一张字条。

sentences.zh: 指挥官说，去把这张字条交给部队，告诉他们，只剩15分钟了。
